LESSON: WRITING 14.5.1 CREATIVE WRITING: DESCRIPTIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.5: Writing 14.5.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 14.5.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which words or expressions do we use to describe things, events or people?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify words and expressions for describing people, places and events
2. write a descriptive composition on people, places and events
3. value the place of description in written and spoken communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 14.5.1 CREATIVE WRITING: DESCRIPTIVE WRITING
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 14.5.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Writing helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 14.5.1 CREATIVE WRITING: DESCRIPTIVE WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify words and expressions for describing people, places and events

What this means
In this part you learn to identify words and expressions for describing people, places and events. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify words and expressions for describing people, places and events.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 14.5.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify words and expressions for describing people, places and events. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write a descriptive composition on people, places and events

What this means
In this part you learn to write a descriptive composition on people, places and events. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a descriptive composition on people, places and events.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 14.5.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a descriptive composition on people, places and events. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Value the place of description in written and spoken communication

What this means
In this part you learn to value the place of description in written and spoken communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value the place of description in written and spoken communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value the place of description in written and spoken communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 14.5.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 14.5.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify words and expressions for describing people, places and events)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 14.5.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Writing to a partner. (skill: write a descriptive composition on people, places and events)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: value the place of description in written and spoken communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 14.5.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify words and expressions for describing people, places and events.
3. Practise this skill: write a descriptive composition on people, places and events.
4. Practise this skill: value the place of description in written and spoken communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 14.5.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 14.5.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Writing 14.5.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which words or expressions do we use to describe things, events or people?
2. How can descriptions make our writing better?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 14.5.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify words and expressions for describing people, places and events.
5. Be able to: write a descriptive composition on people, places and events.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
